items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Nipsie Russell had a bit that he used to use

ctx.x: It was a private joke, and you . . .

Yeah, right. That made me think of that first. But the Lamumba – Nipsie Russell had a bit that he used to use, where he said, during the race for the nuclear physics thing, they had a program going on in Africa where they were going to put something in space. So the Africans were working on a project to put a baboon on the moon. He said you could fly low over this country, and all you could hear was a drum beat, “bing a boom, bing a boom,” and everybody’s humming, saying, “A baboon on the moon by June. A baboon…
